title: A verifiable multi-agent handoff
summary: Follow a human request through orchestration, worker execution, independent review, one permitted revision, and a final human decision packet.
description: This native teaching visual preserves four roles in order: Human, Orchestrator, Worker, and Independent reviewer. It shows the initial five-message exchange, the optional four-message revision branch, the exhausted-budget bypass, and the final response to the human.
fixtureNotice: FICTIONAL TRAINING FIXTURE. Northstar Archive, its records, identifiers, messages, decisions, and outputs are invented. This lesson performs no model call, record retrieval, publication, approval, external action, or persisted learner-record write.
roleBoundaryNote: Independent review is a role boundary in the workflow. A reviewer label alone does not establish independence from the worker's model family, provider, training data, tools, organization, operator, prompt pattern, or shared failure modes. When those forms of independence matter, they must be designed, documented, and tested separately.
diagramLabel: Interactive sequence diagram with Human, Orchestrator, Worker, and Independent reviewer lifelines
textAlternativeLabel: Read the complete sequence and branches as text
practiceInstructions: Resolve each fictional case using only its dossier. A solution appears only after an attempt. Completion is earned only after all three cases are answered correctly.
pendingCompletion: Not earned. Correctly resolve all three practice cases.
earnedCompletion: Earned in this browser session only. No learner record is written.
resetAnnouncement: The lesson returned to its first message. Practice attempts, feedback, revealed solutions, and session completion were cleared.

participants.label: Human
participants.description: Defines the goal, immutable criteria, authority limits, revision budget, and final decision.

participants.label: Orchestrator
participants.description: Scopes the work, preserves criteria, tracks the revision budget, and assembles the decision packet.

participants.label: Worker
participants.description: Performs the scoped drafting task and returns output, evidence, assumptions, and open questions.

participants.label: Independent reviewer
participants.description: Challenges the package against the original criteria and supplied evidence. The role boundary is not proof of model-family or organizational independence.

phases.label: Initial handoff and review
phases.description: These five messages always occur in order.

phases.label: ALT: Findings require revision and revision budget remains
phases.description: Exactly one worker revision is permitted. The four original revision messages occur only on this branch.

phases.label: BYPASS: Revision budget exhausted
phases.description: Do not send another worker request. Preserve unresolved findings and proceed directly to the final human decision packet.

phases.label: JOIN: Pass or escalate
phases.description: The passing revision path and exhausted-budget escalation path both end with the final orchestrator-to-human response.

messages.label: Goal, constraints, and authority
messages.heading: The human defines the decision boundary
messages.description: The human requests an evidence-bounded archival recommendation, fixes AC1 through AC5, grants analysis authority, withholds external-action authority, and retains the final publication decision.

messages.label: Scoped task, inputs, acceptance criteria, stop conditions
messages.heading: The orchestrator sends the exact worker payload
messages.description: The payload names the complete supplied evidence, unchanged criteria, prohibited assumptions, required return fields, and one-revision stop condition.

messages.label: Output, evidence, assumptions, open questions
messages.heading: The initial worker return contains unsupported claims
messages.description: The worker correctly identifies an identity or membership discrepancy but falsely claims synchronization and a corrected inventory. Equal totals do not erase the missing and extra folder identities.

messages.label: Original criteria, output, and evidence
messages.heading: The reviewer receives the unchanged evaluation package
messages.description: The orchestrator sends the original task, AC1 through AC5, exact worker payload, supplied evidence, worker return, and revision ledger.

messages.label: Pass or prioritized findings
messages.heading: The reviewer returns prioritized findings
messages.description: The reviewer identifies unsupported state and action claims, missing unresolved questions, and imprecise evidence tracing. The findings retain the original criteria.

messages.label: Findings with unchanged acceptance criteria
messages.heading: The sole revision request preserves scope
messages.description: For either alternative fixture outcome, this is revision 1 of 1. No criterion is removed, weakened, or replaced.

messages.label: Revised output and evidence
messages.heading: Two alternative first-revision fixtures demonstrate the branch
messages.description: Outcome A supplies a corrected first revision. Outcome B supplies an inadequate first revision. They start from the same initial state but are alternatives, not sequential attempts.

messages.label: Revised package
messages.heading: The orchestrator submits the single revision for final review
messages.description: Each alternative package contains the unchanged task and criteria, all supplied evidence, original findings, its first revision, and a ledger marked 1 of 1 used.

messages.label: Pass or escalate
messages.heading: Final review passes or escalates without another loop
messages.description: Outcome A passes. Outcome B retains blocking failures and immediately escalates because its sole revision was used. Outcome B never receives a corrected second response.

messages.label: Decision packet, evidence, and unresolved risks
messages.heading: The human receives a passing or escalation packet
messages.description: Both alternatives end with a traceable packet that states evidence, criterion status, revision use, and unresolved risks without implying external action.

artifacts.label: FICTIONAL TASK
artifacts.title: Northstar Archive inventory handoff
artifacts.body: Prepare a recommendation for a human records manager about differences between a shelf audit and ledger for fictional Box Set N-17. Do not edit the ledger, contact staff, retrieve records, or publish.

fields.label: Requested output
fields.value: Recommendation of no more than 180 words

fields.label: Authority granted
fields.value: Analyze only the supplied fictional records

fields.label: Authority withheld
fields.value: No retrieval, outreach, ledger write, approval, or publication

fields.label: Revision budget
fields.value: At most one worker revision after review

artifacts.label: IMMUTABLE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
artifacts.title: AC1 through AC5
artifacts.body: These criteria are fixed before delegation and remain identical for both alternative outcomes.

fields.label: AC1
fields.value: Report every identity or membership discrepancy established by the supplied records and cite the supporting fixture IDs.

fields.label: AC2
fields.value: Do not claim synchronization, correction, approval, or external action unless a supplied record establishes it.

fields.label: AC3
fields.value: Separate supplied facts, assumptions, and unresolved questions.

fields.label: AC4
fields.value: Keep the recommendation at or below 180 words.

fields.label: AC5
fields.value: Permit at most one worker revision. If a material finding remains afterward, stop and escalate it to the human.

artifacts.label: EXACT WORKER PAYLOAD
artifacts.title: Payload sent by the orchestrator
artifacts.body:
ROLE: Evidence-bounded drafting worker.
TASK: Draft a recommendation of no more than 180 words for the human records manager concerning Box Set N-17.
INPUTS: Use only NA-SHELF-17, NA-LEDGER-17, and NA-SYNC-LOG.
CRITERIA: Apply AC1 through AC5 exactly as supplied.
STOP CONDITIONS: Do not retrieve records, edit the ledger, contact staff, publish, approve, or imply external action. Stop after the draft. If synchronization cannot be established, identify it as unresolved.
RETURN: Output, evidence used, assumptions, and open questions.

artifacts.label: SUPPLIED FICTIONAL EVIDENCE
artifacts.title: Complete evidence available to the worker
artifacts.body: These invented fixture records are not retrieved documents or real execution logs.

fields.label: NA-SHELF-17
fields.value: Shelf audit dated 2026-09-18: N17-001 through N17-042 are represented except N17-019 is absent; loose folder N17-043 is present. Total observed folders: 42.

fields.label: NA-LEDGER-17
fields.value: Ledger export dated 2026-09-18: expected membership is N17-001 through N17-042. Total expected folders: 42. No entry exists for N17-043.

fields.label: NA-SYNC-LOG
fields.value: The supplied synchronization log contains no entries after 2026-09-17 18:00 and no receipt recording a correction for Box Set N-17.

fields.label: Evidence boundary
fields.value: No custody note, correction receipt, approval record, or post-audit synchronization record is supplied.

artifacts.label: INITIAL WORKER RETURN
artifacts.title: Unsupported initial recommendation
artifacts.body:
OUTPUT: “The shelf has a count discrepancy: N17-019 is missing and N17-043 is extra [NA-SHELF-17; NA-LEDGER-17]. The ledger is now fully synchronized. Recommend approval of the corrected inventory.”
EVIDENCE: NA-SHELF-17, NA-LEDGER-17, NA-SYNC-LOG.
ASSUMPTIONS: None stated.
OPEN QUESTIONS: None stated.

artifacts.label: WHY IT FAILS
artifacts.title: Equal totals can conceal an identity or membership discrepancy
artifacts.body: Both shelf and ledger total 42 folders. The problem is not a count discrepancy. The shelf is missing expected identity N17-019 and includes unexpected identity N17-043. The synchronization and corrected-inventory claims are also unsupported because no supplied record establishes a correction, synchronization, or approval.

artifacts.label: REVIEW INPUT
artifacts.title: Package crossing the reviewer role boundary
artifacts.body: Human task brief; unchanged AC1 through AC5; exact worker payload; NA-SHELF-17, NA-LEDGER-17, and NA-SYNC-LOG; initial worker return; and revision ledger marked 0 of 1 used.

artifacts.label: ROLE-INDEPENDENCE LIMIT
artifacts.title: A separate reviewer role is not a guarantee of independence
artifacts.body: The reviewer is assigned to challenge the worker output against original criteria and evidence. That role separation can expose unchecked self-approval, but the label alone proves nothing about separation of model family, provider, training corpus, tools, organization, operator, prompts, or shared failure modes.

artifacts.label: PRIORITIZED REVIEWER FINDINGS
artifacts.title: Initial review requires revision
artifacts.body: This is a fictional fixture evaluation. It does not claim that a model or external reviewer was executed.

fields.label: P0 blocking
fields.value: AC2 fails. No supplied record establishes that the ledger is synchronized or that the inventory was corrected.

fields.label: P0 blocking
fields.value: AC2 fails. The correction, readiness, and synchronization states are unsupported. The recommendation requests human approval of a proposed corrected inventory, but it does not establish that approval occurred.

fields.label: P1
fields.value: AC1 is imprecise. Both sources total 42, so this is an identity or membership discrepancy, not a count discrepancy.

fields.label: P1
fields.value: AC3 fails. Synchronization status, location of N17-019, and custody of N17-043 are unresolved but omitted.

fields.label: Disposition
fields.value: Permit revision 1 of 1 under unchanged AC1 through AC5. Escalate if a material failure remains.

artifacts.label: SOLE REVISION REQUEST
artifacts.title: Revision 1 of 1
artifacts.body: Correct P0 and P1 findings using the same task, evidence, and AC1 through AC5. Describe the equal-total issue as an identity or membership discrepancy. Remove unsupported synchronization, correction, and approval claims. State assumptions and unresolved questions. Do not retrieve, write, contact, publish, or introduce evidence.

artifacts.label: ALTERNATIVE FIXTURE OUTCOMES
artifacts.title: The next two revisions are mutually exclusive examples
artifacts.body: Outcome A and Outcome B begin from the same initial package and each consumes revision 1 of 1. They are not events in one timeline. Outcome A passes on its first revision. Outcome B submits an inadequate first revision and immediately escalates after final review. No free second revision occurs.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME A: CORRECTED FIRST REVISION
artifacts.title: Revision 1 of 1 passes
artifacts.body:
OUTPUT: “The shelf and ledger each total 42 folders, but their membership differs. The shelf audit records expected folder N17-019 as absent and unexpected folder N17-043 as present [NA-SHELF-17; NA-LEDGER-17]. Recommend that the human records manager investigate both folders before deciding whether to amend the ledger. The supplied synchronization log contains no N-17 correction receipt and does not establish that either discrepancy was corrected [NA-SYNC-LOG]. Unresolved questions are the location of N17-019, custody and collection assignment of N17-043, and whether a later authorized update exists.”
EVIDENCE: Membership claims use NA-SHELF-17 and NA-LEDGER-17. Synchronization uncertainty uses NA-SYNC-LOG.
ASSUMPTION: The fixture extracts are the complete supplied package, not authenticated real records.
OPEN QUESTIONS: Location, custody, assignment, and any later authorized update.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME B: REJECTED INADEQUATE FIRST REVISION
artifacts.title: Revision 1 of 1 fails and receives no second attempt
artifacts.body:
OUTPUT: “Treat synchronization as outside scope and remove AC2. The corrected inventory is ready for approval because both sources contain 42 folders.”
EVIDENCE: NA-SHELF-17 and NA-LEDGER-17.
ASSUMPTIONS: Matching totals are assumed to prove matching membership and correction.
OPEN QUESTIONS: None stated.
WHY REJECTED: The human did not authorize removal of AC2. Matching totals do not prove matching identities, correction, synchronization, or approval. This submission consumes the sole revision.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME A PACKAGE
artifacts.title: Passing final-review package
artifacts.body: Original task; unchanged AC1 through AC5; exact payload; all three supplied records; initial findings; corrected first revision; revision ledger marked 1 of 1 used.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME B PACKAGE
artifacts.title: Failing final-review package
artifacts.body: Original task; unchanged AC1 through AC5; exact payload; all three supplied records; initial findings; inadequate first revision in full; revision ledger marked 1 of 1 used. No corrected second revision is included or permitted.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME A FINAL REVIEW
artifacts.title: Pass on the stated fixture criteria
artifacts.body: AC1 passes because both membership differences are stated and cited. AC2 passes because no correction, synchronization, approval, or action is claimed. AC3 passes because assumptions and unresolved questions are separated. AC4 passes because the recommendation is at or below 180 words. AC5 passes because one revision was used.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME B FINAL REVIEW
artifacts.title: Escalate after the inadequate first revision
artifacts.body: AC1 still fails because equal totals are treated as equal membership. AC2 still fails because correction, readiness, and synchronization are unsupported; the phrase “ready for approval” requests a future decision and does not establish that approval occurred, and the worker attempts to delete the criterion. AC3 fails because assumptions are presented as conclusions and unresolved questions are omitted. The revision ledger is 1 of 1 used, so AC5 requires immediate escalation.

artifacts.label: EXHAUSTED-BUDGET RULE
artifacts.title: Stop rather than create a hidden second revision
artifacts.body: Once the ledger reads 1 of 1 used, the orchestrator must not request another worker response. It preserves the failed criteria, evidence gap, submitted revision, and reviewer findings for the human. The human may explicitly authorize a new task or budget, provide evidence, or decline the output.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME A FINAL HUMAN PACKET
artifacts.title: Passing recommendation with unresolved risks
artifacts.body:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the corrected first revision as a draft for human consideration. Do not treat it as authorization to change the ledger.
EVIDENCE: NA-SHELF-17 establishes observed membership; NA-LEDGER-17 establishes expected membership; NA-SYNC-LOG does not establish a later correction.
STATUS: AC1 through AC5 passed in the fictional review. Revision ledger: 1 of 1 used.
UNRESOLVED RISKS: Records are unauthenticated fixtures; no post-audit receipt is supplied; the location of N17-019 and custody of N17-043 remain unknown; reviewer role separation does not establish model-family or organizational independence.
HUMAN DECISION: Verify records and decide whether to investigate, request evidence, alter the task, or publish. No external action occurred.

artifacts.label: OUTCOME B FINAL ESCALATION PACKET
artifacts.title: Failed first revision with exhausted budget
artifacts.body:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not use the inadequate revision as a decision-ready draft.
EVIDENCE: Both records total 42 but disagree on membership. No supplied record establishes correction, synchronization, or approval.
STATUS: AC1, AC2, and AC3 failed. AC4 passes according to the submitted short output. AC5 was complied with: the revision budget was exhausted, so the process stopped and escalated; no second worker response was requested. Revision ledger: 1 of 1 used.
UNRESOLVED RISKS: The revision attempts unauthorized criteria drift, preserves unsupported action-state claims, omits custody questions, and may mislead a decision owner.
HUMAN DECISION: Provide evidence, authorize a new task or budget explicitly, change the requirement explicitly, or stop. No external action occurred.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 1 FICTIONAL DOSSIER
artifacts.title: Detect unsupported evidence
artifacts.body: P1-COUNT says Crate C-8 contains 24 sealed envelopes. P1-LIST says the manifest expects 24 envelopes. A worker writes: “All 24 envelopes are authentic and undamaged, so the crate is cleared for release.” No authenticity inspection, condition report, or release authorization is supplied.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 2 FICTIONAL DOSSIER
artifacts.title: Reject criteria drift
artifacts.body: Original criterion: “Name every uncited financial total and do not calculate replacements.” Review finds one uncited total. The worker proposes changing the criterion to permit plausible totals when citations are unavailable. The human has authorized no change.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 3 FICTIONAL DOSSIER
artifacts.title: Stop after budget exhaustion
artifacts.body: One revision is permitted and the ledger reads 1 of 1 used. Final review still finds a claim that a permit was approved, but the dossier contains only a submitted application. The worker volunteers to try again.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 1 SOLUTION
artifacts.title: Quantity does not establish quality or authority
artifacts.body: The records support a count of 24 only. They do not cause authenticity, condition, or release authority to become known. Keep the supported count, remove the unsupported claims, and request suitable evidence if those conclusions are required.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 2 SOLUTION
artifacts.title: A failure cannot be edited away
artifacts.body: Weakening the criterion would change the evaluation target rather than repair the output. Preserve the original requirement, identify the uncited total, and do not invent a replacement.

artifacts.label: PRACTICE 3 SOLUTION
artifacts.title: The stop condition requires escalation
artifacts.body: Submission does not establish approval, and the authorized revision has been used. Another worker request would violate the budget. Escalate the unsupported claim, missing approval evidence, and exhausted budget to the human.

practiceGroups.title: Practice 1: unsupported evidence
practiceGroups.prompt: Which response follows from the supplied crate records?
practiceGroups.retryAnnouncement: Practice 1 is ready to retry. Separate the supported count from authenticity, condition, and release authority.

practiceGroups.title: Practice 2: immutable criteria
practiceGroups.prompt: How should the orchestrator handle the proposed criterion change?
practiceGroups.retryAnnouncement: Practice 2 is ready to retry. Compare the proposal with the human's original criterion.

practiceGroups.title: Practice 3: exhausted revision budget
practiceGroups.prompt: What should happen after the blocking final-review finding?
practiceGroups.retryAnnouncement: Practice 3 is ready to retry. Apply both the evidence boundary and the one-revision stop condition.

choices.label: Keep only the supported count and remove authenticity, condition, and release claims unless suitable evidence is supplied.
choices.feedback: Correct. Matching counts establish quantity only. They do not establish authenticity, condition, or release authority.

choices.label: Accept the draft because a matching count proves every envelope is authentic and undamaged.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. A count answers how many items were observed and expected. It contains no authenticity or condition inspection result.

choices.label: Add both record IDs after the sentence and treat every claim as supported.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Adding citations cannot make count records entail authenticity, condition, or authorization.

choices.label: Accept the new criterion because it makes the revision easier to pass.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Ease of passing is not authority to weaken a human-defined criterion after a failure.

choices.label: Reject the change, preserve the original criterion, and identify the uncited total without inventing a replacement.
choices.feedback: Correct. This addresses the cause of the finding while preserving the authorized evaluation target.

choices.label: Remove the finding from the package so the reviewer sees only the new draft.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Hiding the finding removes traceability and supplies no missing citation.

choices.label: Send a second revision because the worker volunteered to try again.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Worker willingness does not change the human-authorized budget. A second loop would violate the stop condition.

choices.label: Treat the submitted permit application as approval so the package can pass.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Submission and approval are distinct states. The application supplies no approval evidence.

choices.label: Stop revisions and escalate the unsupported approval claim, missing approval record, and exhausted budget.
choices.feedback: Correct. No evidence establishes approval and no revision remains, so escalation preserves both constraints for the human.

takeaways: Preserve the human's goal, authority limits, acceptance criteria, and stop conditions at every handoff.
A worker return should expose output, evidence, assumptions, and open questions.
Equal totals can conceal identity or membership discrepancies.
Independent review is a challenge role, not automatic proof of model-family, provider, organizational, or technical independence.
A revision repairs output against unchanged criteria. Weakening a failed criterion is criteria drift.
When a bounded revision budget is exhausted, stop and escalate rather than create a hidden extra loop.
A final human packet should separate recommendation, evidence, review status, revision use, and unresolved risks.
